This app helps you catalog your retro games, consoles and accessories collection, with automatic photo recognition and price estimates.

Tap the + button to add an item: scan a barcode (games only), take a photo (games, consoles and accessories), pick one from your gallery, or enter everything manually. The app tries to automatically recognize the name, type and associated console.

For better recognition, crop the photo tightly on the logo or title, avoid glare and blur — the sharper and more readable the text, the more reliable automatic identification will be. For a game found via online search, the main photo shown will be the real cover art.

Browse the catalog of consoles and accessories, discover their best-known games, add a console, accessory or game straight to your collection or wishlist from its page, and add your own custom entry (with a photo) if one is missing, via the + button.

The Wishlist tab lists your future acquisitions. The Total tab shows the estimated value of your whole collection, updated automatically. If no comparable eBay listing is found, an AI suggests an estimate instead, marked "(AI)" next to the price — less reliable than a real listing, just a rough ballpark.

Back up your whole collection (data and photos) to a file you choose where to save, and restore it anytime — useful after a crash or a reinstall. Tip: in settings (gear icon), you can also change the app\'s background image.
In settings (gear icon), a "Tips" tab summarizes advice for framing your photos well and naming items well in manual entry, for more reliable recognition and value estimates.

The Games tab (the controller) offers retro mini-games. Retro Tennis is free from the start; play Quiz and unlocked games to earn 💎 points. The very first time you launch each game, a screen explains the rules and how to play. After a game, an optional ad triples the points you earned; the Games tab also offers a Daily Chest (ad) with bonus points every 24 hours.

With your points, open the Shop (icon top-right, or button in the Games tab) to unlock more games, visual themes (Time Travel, Galaxy, Treasure Hunt, Ectoplasm…) and options (Excel export, reduced ads, full Premium access). Once a theme is purchased, apply it in settings (gear icon) → Theme tab.
📚 Scan a whole batch at once

To add several items at once (a shelf, a lot), choose "📚 Scan a batch" from the + menu. An AI analyzes the whole photo, isolates each detected game or console and shows you a checklist: uncheck any mistakes, then confirm to add everything at once to your collection or wishlist. Cover, description, genre, and year are automatically looked up and filled in for each added game. Tip: a well-lit photo where each title is clearly readable gives the best results. Batch scanning is reserved for Premium or unlocked by watching an ad before taking the photo (single-item scanning stays free).

When adding or editing a console, game, or accessory, paste a link (Wikipedia page, product page…) into the "Source URL" field, then tap "🔗 Import from URL": the app fetches the title, description, year and photo to automatically fill in any fields still empty — never overwriting what you\'ve already entered.

For an accessory, fill in its "Associated console": the catalog and online search then prioritize the right results for that console (e.g. the Master System\'s Control Stick, the Super Nintendo\'s Super Scope). Game & Watch tip: type "Game & Watch" as the console name to open the full list of models (Ball, Fire, Donkey Kong, Zelda, Panorama and Table Top series, reissues…), each linked to its Encyclopedia entry with its real photo and real Wikipedia link.

From settings (gear icon) → Backup, import an Excel (.xlsx) or CSV file from an existing collection, even if its columns don\'t match the app\'s format: just tell us which column corresponds to each field (name, platform, condition, price…), check the preview of detected items, then confirm the import.

In the Encyclopedia, tap the ✅ icon at the top right to turn on multi-select: check off several consoles or accessories, then add them all at once to your collection or wishlist with the bar that appears at the bottom.
No other lead detected on this photo.

Frame the photo tightly on the logo or title, avoid reflections and blur — the sharper and more legible the text, the more reliable the automatic recognition. If the result isn\'t right, two options: the "🔄 Retry" button tries another lead detected on the same photo (another visible text), without re-cropping; the "✂️ Crop" button starts over from the original photo, lets you crop it differently, then re-runs a full analysis.
🏷️ Naming an item well in manual entry

If automatic photo recognition finds nothing for a game, console, or accessory, you can type the name by hand. In that case, try to find the item on PriceCharting and use the exact same name used there: the estimated value will be more accurate, since price lookup relies on matching the name.

When no comparable eBay listing is found, the app asks an AI to search online for a plausible used price instead. This price is marked "(AI)" next to the amount: it\'s an estimate, less reliable than a real eBay listing, just a rough ballpark. You can always correct it manually via "Edit price".

In the Encyclopedia, the 📰 icon in the top right opens a feed of upcoming retro gaming news: reissued consoles, collector packs, arcade cabinets, game releases... Each item links back to its original source ("View source" button) and displays automatically in your language. The feed updates itself, nothing to do on your end.
In the Encyclopedia (Consoles tab), a second menu next to "Sort by" lets you filter by type: home consoles, handheld consoles, or computers.
In the Encyclopedia, tap directly on a console or accessory thumbnail to see it enlarged; tap the enlarged image (or outside it) to close it.

How it works: the app first reads the text in the photo (fast, offline); if it's ambiguous, a visual AI analyzes the image (logos, cover art). If the AI service is overloaded, a backup one automatically takes over — you don't have to do anything.

SINGLE photo (one item): frame tightly on the cover art or logo, flat and face-on (avoid angles), in good light with no glare or blur. Just one item in the frame.

BATCH scan (multiple items): lay the boxes/games face up, aligned and not stacked, so each title is readable at a glance. Good, even lighting, no glare. Limit yourself to about 10-15 items per photo: two sharp photos are better than one overloaded shot where titles overlap.

If the result isn't right: "🔄 Retry" suggests another lead without re-cropping, "✂️ Crop" restarts a full analysis with a new crop.
